citations.assessment: The Yerushalmi gives the wedding imagery, the angel’s confirmation, the fire around the sages, the trees and the kiss. The Bavli gives the parallel fire, singing trees and blessing, with differences in narration.

citations.assessment: The two images are applied together to Elazar ben Arakh in the praise of the disciples.
The Mishnah explicitly lists five disciples and Elazar’s spring image and preserves alternative scales of praise.
The internal contrast describes the Great Rabbi Eliezer as Sinai and Elazar ben Arakh as uprooting mountains. It does not by itself identify the abbreviated external work.
The dialogue explicitly has Rabbi Yehoshua ask Rabbi Akiva about Elazar ben Arakh’s days. Heilprin supplies his own chronological inference.
The comparison is to another internal Kalir identification. It does not settle which Elazar was the poet.

The digital midrash gives Emmaus, his wife’s food-container analogy and his failure to answer a question about bread with relish. Heilprin paraphrases the unanswered question as the name of the relish.

The Bavli gives the misreading and restoration of his learning. The preceding segment gives the wine and water; the continuation gives the Nehorai alternatives. No illness-and-recovery opening appears in the Bavli text.
The reciprocal dossier recounts the Emmaus and Diyomset sources separately.
The Mishnah’s Nehorai maxim is also explicitly quoted by the cited Shabbat passage.
The internal dossier catalogues competing names and explicitly considers the chronological objections.

The Chida attributes a strongly parallel interpretation to Shimshon of Ostropoli, including רי״ב, 605 and כד״ת. It is comparison evidence for the attribution, not a transcription of Heilprin’s source or a resolution of all three Yalkut references.

notes.text: The exact Yuchasin wording for acute in argument remains open. Compared Avot de-Rabbi Natan and Avot. They attest the spring image without proving the secondary gloss.
The Asarah Ma’amarot expansion and precise locus remain provisional. The internal Eliezer comparison uses the same abbreviation without expanding it.
Heilprin’s claim of earlier death remains an inference with a compressed referent. The Tosefta contrasts the times rhetorically; it does not explicitly date either death.
Preserve the reported possible Kalir identification as an attributed option. Compared the rival identification in Heilprin’s Elazar son of Shimon dossier and the separate heading for the poet.
Toledot 50a requires a primary image or exact text in the cited edition. The Chida discusses the tradition and cites this section; the precise Yalkut witness was not authenticated.
Bo 89 remains edition-dependent and unverified. Targeted digital and scan discovery did not establish this exact primary passage.
The alphabetical section’s exact witness remains open. The collected parallels do not establish the edition, section and wording of this locator.

The direct Tzefunei Tziyyoni text and exact attribution remain unresolved. The Chida quotes the interpretive tradition in Petach Einayim. Search results alone cannot establish the earlier text’s details.

The reported encounter and its intended cross-reference are unresolved. The cited Elazar/Shabbat and Chagigah passages do not supply such an encounter. Preserve Heilprin’s explicit chronological surprise.

The primary edition of the Damascus synagogue responsum remains to be collated. A bibliography lead points to Mabit volume III, responsum 99, folio 147c. The alternate label comes from a published quotation. Bounded primary lookup did not return a usable witness; preserve Heilprin’s part and section layout as written.

The siglum’s expansion, exact geographic witness, listed tombs and local site attributions remain open. Compared Adler’s separate travel account. It gives a shorter roster and cannot establish the wording of Gelilot Eretz Yisrael.
The other locus, place reading and possible two Rav Hunas remain provisional. Neither the scope of the other citation nor its intended Rav Huna is established by the nearby burial lists.
